headline: Updated school policies on employee electronic monitoring, reference checks, bloodborne pathogens, and student restraint presented.
summary: The employee monitoring policy follows changes to state law section 31-48d, and new hires on or after October 1 will get a plain-language notice of prohibited activities and monitoring locations. Physical restraint and seclusion rules now require parents to be told the same day, under Public Act 26-1, instead of within 24 hours. The reference check policy adds optional language on out-of-state registry checks, and the bloodborne pathogen policy adds an exposure plan as an appendix. The revised policies go through consent in two weeks.
discussion: Computer system monitoring: A question was raised whether a teacher's personal phone on school Wi-Fi falls under the policy. The answer given was technically yes, and new hires will get the notice as part of their paperwork.

Out-of-state reference checks: The optional language would allow DCF registry checks and similar checks on out-of-state applicants where possible. Some favored adding it, but wanted the full board to weigh in first.
Bloodborne pathogen training: Discussion noted that all certified and non-certified staff take this training every school year, as a required training.
